interpretation: Actual native local owner selection is bounded to 16 initialized width bytes, using one q load and in-register widened prefix/comparison/reduction. Same exact query population, different order: blocked processes all 256 probes per geometry block; scattered uses full-domain query permutation and rebinds/loads extent per query. Common hash, runtime divisions, owner stores and checksum are charged.

Every native sample is faster than every baseline sample at 16M for both before/after shrink and both blocked/scattered families, across two reciprocal process orders and two repetitions each.

Compact width geometry and fewer dependent checkpoint steps plausibly matter to scattered performance; same-format scalar/native pairing establishes the advantage for the composed trace. The capture does not isolate branch misses, LLC/DRAM service or an architecture-specific instruction cause.
